From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline and subprocessor list (NovaMed) — Security review notes

Thanks for the ping — I reviewed NovaMed's redline and the subprocessor CSV. High-level: their telemetry carve-out language is reasonable if we tighten the definition and add explicit exclusions. Key Security asks: 

- Define "aggregated performance metrics" (we should list examples: token latency histograms, error-rate %, avg throughput) and explicitly exclude request/response bodies, prompt/response embeddings, and user identifiers.
- Retention cap: propose we agree to a 90-day retention window for aggregated metrics used for product ops; anything used for debugging can be retained for 14 days and then deleted unless a customer-approved incident retention is requested.
- No-training warranty: we can sign a contractual "no training" clause for NovaMed-managed data, but must qualify it with an operational note: if a customer opts-in to a training program we will record that separately and require an amendment and explicit opt-in.
- Subprocessors: the CSV has two names that map to our monitoring vendor not already on the public list; need procurement confirmation that those vendors have SOC2 and a data processing addendum.

I'll draft precise redline text for Security to propose (short edits to section 3.2 and a new clause 8.4 for telemetry). That draft will include the 90/14 day retention proposal and the training carve-out wording.

-Olga
Director, Product Security

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline and subprocessor list (NovaMed) — Product impact

Quick product/ops take after reading Olga's notes:

- Telemetry carve-out: we can provide the aggregated metrics they want without collecting PII or full prompt/response payloads. We already emit token latency distributions, 95/99 p99 latencies, error-rate by route, and throughput by model. I recommend committing to a minimal retained metrics set (latency histograms, error-rate, avg throughput) at 90 days.
- Implementation: minor changes to our metrics masking to ensure payloads are never stored in the aggregated pipeline. We may need a short infra change to formally redact sampling traces; estimate 2 engineer-weeks to push a guarded workflow and add test coverage.
- No-training clause: product stance is fine with a contractual "no training" on NovaMed inputs/responses unless they sign an explicit training consent. Note: we must add a UI/ops flag to record consent if this is later requested (low priority, 3-4 engineer-weeks).

If Security approves the suggested redline text, Product is OK to sign off on the carve-out with the 90/14 day retention windows and the implementation effort noted. Please confirm and I will prepare the short technical note for Legal to include.

-Karthik
Senior PM, Serving Runtime

Asha/Kevin — thanks for the DPA and the list. Internal review complete: Security and Product propose the following agreement terms and operational notes (to be incorporated into your redline):

1) Telemetry carve-out: Redwood will accept an aggregated-performance-metrics carve-out limited to latency histograms, error-rate %, and average throughput by model/route. We will explicitly exclude any request or response bodies, embeddings, or user-identifiers.
2) Retention: aggregated metrics retained for 90 days. Short-term debugging traces retained for up to 14 days and purged automatically unless a customer-approved incident retention request is made.
3) No-training warranty: Redwood will warrant we will not use NovaMed inputs or outputs to train models without an explicit, documented opt-in amendment.
4) Subprocessors: we flagged two monitoring vendors not on our public list. We will provide SOC2 attestations for those vendors and confirm DPA attachments; if any vendor is unacceptable we will work through an exception process.

We're prepared to accept these items as edits to the DPA. Attached: Security's proposed redline snippets and the subprocessor notes. Please let us know if this maps to your legal team's expectations; if so, send the DocuSign link and Legal will circulate for signature — our target is to have this executed within 3 business days.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
